message.content:
The quadratic equation  

\[
3x^{2}-2x-5=0
\]

has roots found by the quadratic formula \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}\).

Here \(a=3,\; b=-2,\; c=-5\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
x &= \frac{-(-2)\pm\sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4(3)(-5)}}{2(3)} \\
  &= \frac{2\pm\sqrt{4+60}}{6} \\
  &= \frac{2\pm\sqrt{64}}{6} \\
  &= \frac{2\pm 8}{6}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{x=\frac{5}{3}\quad\text{or}\quad x=-1}.
\]
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Solve for the roots of the equation 3x^2 - 2x - 5." They want the roots of the quadratic equation 3x^2 - 2x - 5 = 0. Solve using quadratic formula: x = [2 ± sqrt(4 + 60)]/(2*3) = [2 ± sqrt(64)]/6 = [2 ± 8]/6. So x = (2+8)/6 = 10/6 = 5/3, or x = (2-8)/6 = -6/6 = -1. So roots are x = 5/3 and x = -1.

We can provide that. No tool needed.
